clue.text: Fraud taken to court for hearing

indicators.note: for hearing asks us to take the sound of the words when spoken, not their spelling

parts.note: someone taken to court has been sued

explanation.surface: A con man ends up in front of a judge for his trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The P of this word is silent, so it is said just like SUED. A PSEUD is British slang for a pretentious fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseud is a pretentious person, a sham or impostor, so a kind of fraud.

clue.text: No oil painting alluded to in rhyme

definitions.text: No oil painting alluded to in rhyme

parts.words: No oil painting alluded to in rhyme
parts.note: a homely-looking woman, named in a jingle whose two halves rhyme

explanation.definitionFit: A plain Jane is an unattractive woman, someone no oil painting, a phrase whose words rhyme.

clue.text: Insist on being totally accurate

definitions.meaning: to demand something, as in to require payment

explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand insistently, and exact also means precise or correct.

clue.text: Whacked as boxer might be?

definitions.meaning: a boxer is a breed of dog, which could be tired

explanation.definitionFit: Dog-tired means utterly exhausted, and a weary boxer dog would literally be a tired dog.

clue.text: Actor, virtually disdainful, making hypocrite out of Dickens

parts.note: Gregory Peck was a Hollywood film actor

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word for disdainful is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: sniffy means scornful or disdainful

explanation.surface: A snooty performer is turned into a two-faced character from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth Pecksniff is the sanctimonious hypocrite in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecksniff is the oily, preaching humbug of Martin Chuzzlewit, a byword for hypocrisy.

clue.text: Encourage husband to drink up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Urge a man to finish his drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To push someone is to urge or encourage them on.

clue.text: One rabbiting on about reputedly mad person on TV

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
the phrase mad as a hatter makes a hatter reputedly mad
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A talkative person discusses a supposed lunatic on the television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbiting on' is British for talking at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is someone who talks incessantly, rabbiting on.

clue.text: Fashionable spot to hold game

indicators.note: to hold means the word for spot surrounds the game

parts.note: to spot is to spy or catch sight of
snap is a children's card game

explanation.surface: A trendy place where a match is staged.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy, as in a snappy dresser, means smart and stylish.

clue.text: Usually wanting lager — nine drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Short of beer, after nine pints have been downed.
explanation.definitionFit: In general is an idiom meaning on the whole, as a rule, usually.

clue.text: All the buses get away on time

parts.note: to flee is to get away

explanation.surface: Every bus departs punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet is the full set of vehicles a company runs, so all its buses.

clue.text: Relief of pain in a leg as a result of treatment?

indicators.note: a result of treatment reworks the letters of the preceding words into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor's question about whether a numbed leg comes from therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result of treatment' rearranges IN A LEG AS A into the medical word for pain relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for absence or relief of pain, as from painkillers.

clue.text: Point of view of old invader

definitions.meaning: a standpoint or slant from which something is seen
one of the Germanic people who invaded and settled Britain after the Romans left

explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a viewpoint, and the Angles were invaders of post-Roman Britain who gave England its name.

clue.text: Fool after money has turned over card

indicators.note: turned over signals that the word for money is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: tin is slang for money
a card is a witty, amusing person, a wit

explanation.surface: An idiot chases cash after flipping a playing card.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN reversed gives NIT; then WIT, since a 'card' is a joker or wit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a stupid person, a synonym for fool.

clue.text: Can old favourites you've backed go faster?

indicators.note: backed signals that the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a can is a tin
pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: A punter asks whether the elderly horses they bet on can speed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you've backed' turns the whole run around; in the surface 'backed' looks like betting language and 'old favourites' like horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom urging a driver to press the accelerator, so to hurry or go faster.

clue.text: I was the last person to win this

definitions.text: I was the last person to win this

parts.words: I was the last person to win this
parts.note: a joke award handed to whoever finishes in last place

explanation.definitionFit: A booby prize is a consolation award given to the competitor who comes last.

clue.text: Fairly and squarely at the top of the table?

definitions.meaning: openly and honestly, with nothing hidden

definitions.text: at the top of the table?
definitions.meaning: read literally, positioned over a board or table

explanation.definitionFit: Above board means honest and open, and literally describes something placed over a board or table.

clue.text: Title of novel The End of Brighton Pier Show

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a fresh order
The End of picks the last letter of Brighton

explanation.surface: The name of a book about the end of a seaside entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the end of Brighton, joins PIER SHOW, and 'novel' rearranges the nine letters. Brighton Pier is a seaside pier on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Title in law means a right to own property, so ownership.

clue.text: Tease sent to cold bed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A child who teases is sent off to a chilly bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is a child's cot, a small bed with barred sides.

clue.text: What's tough coming up day before closing date?

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a yob is a young thug or tough
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
the end is the closing

explanation.surface: What's difficult about the day before a deadline?
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing date' looks like a deadline, but 'date' is the definition. YOB is British for a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is someone you go out with romantically, such as a boyfriend.

clue.text: Reveal Havana to be off-limits?

parts.note: a Havana is a Cuban cigar, something to smoke
out means not allowed, off-limits

explanation.surface: Show that Cuban cigars are banned.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoke out is to force something hidden into the open, so to reveal or expose it.

clue.text: Wise chap I ignored is a flyer in the main

indicators.note: ignored means the letter I is left out of the name

parts.note: Ernie Wise was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A clever fellow who overlooks something is a bird over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' is not clever here: it names the comedian Ernie Wise. 'the main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, a bird that flies over the main, or ocean.

clue.text: Partner introducing bishop to girl oddly

indicators.note: introducing means the other pieces are put inside the word for partner

parts.note: an ally is a partner or associate
B is the chess notation for bishop
Norma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone's partner awkwardly presents a clergyman to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormally means in an unusual way, so strangely or oddly.

clue.text: Drunkard hanging round clubs is a northerner

indicators.note: hanging round means the drunkard surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a souse is a drunk
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A drinker loitering near nightspots is from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: A SCOUSE is someone from Liverpool, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouse is an informal name for a Liverpudlian, a native of the north-west of England.

clue.text: Firm's fake -e-mail, say, printed out

parts.note: firm means hard; the 's is a link
a copy is a fake or imitation

explanation.surface: A company's forged message is put on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard copy is a printed paper version of an electronic document such as an e-mail.

clue.text: Colouring like Will S's wife when upset?

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Shakespeare's wife was Anne Hathaway; shortened like Will S, she becomes Anne H

explanation.surface: A dye compared to an upset Mrs Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like Will S' tells you to cut the wife's surname to its initial as Shakespeare's is.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye used for colouring hair and skin.

clue.text: Winter sportsman who's taken against idle so-and-so

indicators.note: who's taken means the skier holds the next piece inside

parts.note: a skier takes part in a winter sport
V, for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A snow athlete has turned on a lazy person.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIVER is British slang for someone who dodges work or school.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiver is a shirker who avoids work, so an idle layabout.

clue.text: Bill's not popular, say

indicators.note: not means the word for popular is removed

parts.note: an invoice is a bill; the 's is a link
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A proposed law is unpopular, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is a commercial bill here, not draft legislation; 'say' is a noun, as in having a say.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a voice in something means having a say in it.

clue.text: Extremely sharp boy, was 8

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of sharp

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A very clever lad was quick.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to the answer at 8 down, FLEET, so 'was 8' means was fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fleet is to be swift, so someone who was fleet sped along.

clue.text: Some entrepreneur henceforth backing PM

indicators.note: backing means that part is read backwards
some means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Part of a business leader's future is to support the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, the run URHEN across 'entrepreneur henceforth' gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister.

clue.text: VIP is more prepared to make do

indicators.note: prepared means these letters are made ready again in a new order

explanation.surface: An important guest is better equipped to cope.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to make do with whatever is to hand, without preparation.

clue.text: Be terribly afraid of nick

definitions.meaning: an old sense: to dread or fear something
British slang for arrest, as police do

explanation.definitionFit: Apprehend once meant to fear, the root of apprehensive, and now means to arrest a suspect.

clue.text: Flower pot found at back of hut?

indicators.note: at back of picks out the last letter of hut

parts.note: pot and weed are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A plant pot turns up behind a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows, a river; the Tweed runs along the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a flower is a river, and the Tweed is one.
